rich_summary: Krishna (Kesava) reveals a terrifying divine manifestation in the Kuru court after Duryodhana’s defiance. From his blazing body emerge countless gods, celestial beings, weapons, and heroes, while flames and sparks radiate from every pore. Most kings shut their eyes in fear, but sages and a few wise elders are granted divine sight to behold the cosmic form. After the earth trembles and celestial drums sound, Krishna withdraws the vision and departs the court. Dhritarashtra insists he sought peace, but Krishna points out that Duryodhana rejected all counsel. He then visits Kunti, recounts the failed diplomacy, and asks what message he should carry to the Pandavas. Kunti urges Yudhishthira to remember his Kshatriya duty and not let passive virtue prevent rightful action.

highlight_spans.why: Krishna bursts into divine laughter and begins revealing his cosmic nature.
The emergence of countless gods from Krishna’s body emphasizes his identity as the cosmic source of all divinity.
The fearful reaction of the assembled kings underscores the overwhelming power of Krishna’s revelation.
Krishna formally states that Duryodhana rejected all wise counsel, marking the failure of the peace mission.
Kunti’s speech reframes the conflict as a matter of Kshatriya duty, challenging Yudhishthira’s excessive attachment to passive virtue.

top_scenes.scene_text: Krishna in the Kuru court radiating a blazing cosmic form as tiny radiant gods, weapons, and flames emerge from every part of his body while terrified kings recoil.
Celestial drums sounding and flowers raining from the sky as the earth trembles while sages and a few elders gaze upon Krishna’s divine manifestation.
Krishna meeting Kunti in her chamber as she speaks sternly about a king’s duty, urging Yudhishthira to uphold Kshatriya valor.
